messages:
Marta Singh: Heads-up — enterprise tenant ACME wants a tenant-specific canary that never touches shared pools and has an automatic failover to their older model if latency or error rate spikes. Can we sketch a proposal?
Drew Patel: Quick Q — is this strictly Dedicated customers only? or should dedicated+private share same config surface?
Marta Singh: Dedicated only for now. They signed up for isolation guarantees.
Jen Lo: Also need quota/throughput caps per-tenant at canary stage. ACME asked for max 10 rps during ramp and circuit-break at 5% 1m error-rate.
Samir Rao: From runtime side we can do per-tenant routing keys + isolated worker pools. The tricky part is traffic-splitting semantics: % of sessions vs % of requests. Which do we want?
Marta Singh: They want session-consistent split (sticky routing) so a session stays on the canary variant for duration.
Leo Chen: Sticky session + isolated pools = increased resource footprint. Need clear failover plan: if canary pool degrades, redirect all sticky sessions to fallback model variant in their dedicated pool, not shared.
Maria Ortega: UX ask from Console: allow operators to define tenant slice, session-stickiness, ramp windows, and automated rollback thresholds. Prefer templates for enterprise.
Drew Patel: Proposal sketch (config proto):
```
tenant_canary: {
  tenant_id: "acme",
  session_split_pct: 10,
  max_rps: 10,
  isolation: "dedicated_pool",
  fallback_model: "acme-v1",
  circuit_break_thresholds: {error_rate_1m: 0.05, p95_latency_ms: 1200},
  ramp_seconds: 1800
}
```
Jen Lo: Love that. Suggest adding "telemetry_tags": ["tenant:acme","canary"] so dashboards auto-surface metrics.
Samir Rao: Implementation note: runtime needs to surface per-tenant in-flight counters and token burn to prevent noisy neighbor within the dedicated pool. Add max_inflight_per_tenant.
Marta Singh: Ok add it. Also add "graceful_drain_seconds" for rollback.
Leo Chen: Fallback semantics: do we retry in the control plane, or drop and let client retry? For low-latency apps we should failover synchronously.
Maria Ortega: Console UX — show a one-line status for tenant canary: percent, health (green/amber/red), active rollbacks, last fallback reason. Clicking expands timeline and recent alerts.
Drew Patel: Telemetry requirements: p50/p95/p99 latency, 1m error-rate, model-quality regressions (eval set score), cost-per-token deltas. Need alerting thresholds mapped to rollback policies.
Samir Rao: On API debate: Should this be a first-class Rollout resource or a TenantPolicy with a canary field? I vote TenantPolicy — fits enterprise model and can hold ACLs.
Marta Singh: TenantPolicy seems cleaner for permissions, but Rollout resource can be reused for non-tenant canaries. Tradeoffs.
Jen Lo: For visibility, console should render both paths identically. API can be flexible: create Rollout but link to tenant_id and generate TenantPolicy pointers.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: Canary config uploaded for tenant=acme by @marta at 1993456802. Validation checks: schema ok, quotas within limits.
Leo Chen: OpsBot caught one: runtime validation flagged missing max_inflight_per_tenant.
Marta Singh: Fixed and re-uploading.
Marta Singh: For safety guards: require a minimum healthy-check throughput before ramp (eg 20 successful requests within last 5m) and an SLO breach multiplier — if SLO >1.5x baseline, auto-rollback.
Drew Patel: Also add circuit-breaker cooldown: if triggered, lock canary for 10m and reduce split to 0 before allowing re-ramp.
Maria Ortega: For dashboards: auto-create transient panel for canaries with filters: tenant_id, rollout_id, timeframe. Also put a small 'cost delta' sparkline.
Samir Rao: Runtime TODOs: - implement per-tenant sticky routing key - enforce per-tenant inflight & rps caps - fast failover path that swaps routing map atomically - emit canary lifecycle events to telemetry stream
Jen Lo: Ops playbook note: when rollback occurs, page on-call and include reason + last 100 request ids for the tenant.
Marta Singh: Follow-ups: I'll draft a PR with the API proto, console mockups, and a rough runtime implementation plan. Targeting RFC by EOD Thursday. Any blockers?
Drew Patel: Resource ask: may need 2 extra GPU slots to stage an isolated canary environment for smoke tests.
Leo Chen: Acknowledged. I'll check capacity and reserve if available.
Maria Ortega: I'll mock the console panels and tenant template.
Samir Rao: I'll prototype the routing map change logic and event emission.
Jen Lo: I'll write the playbook snippets and alert mapping.
Marta Singh: Thanks everyone. If you have docs or sketches, drop them in #eng-platform/design-links.
OpsBot: note: thread archived to project=tenant-safety after 2hr inactivity.
